How a project runs

From first call to launch day.

  1. Talk it throughWe learn how your organisation works today and what you want to change.
  2. Scope and quoteYou receive a written list of what will be built and the price before work starts.
  3. Build and reviewYou see working versions along the way and tell us what to adjust.
  4. Train and launchWe train your staff, move your existing records in and go live.
  5. SupportWe stay available for fixes, questions and new features.

About

A Kampala software company for working organisations.

Ron | tech hub is a software company based in Uganda. We build websites and the systems that schools, shops and hospitals depend on every day: school management, point of sale and hospital management, along with custom software for everything else.

Our tagline is Smart Solutions, Powerful Systems, Endless Possibilities. In practice that means we choose the simplest system that solves your problem, build it to hold up under daily use, and leave room for it to grow when your organisation does.

We work closely with the people who will use the system. A cashier, a bursar and a records clerk each know things about the job that a specification never captures, so we ask them.

What guides the work

Three habits behind every project.

Keep it simple

Screens that new staff understand on the first day, with only the buttons they need.

Write it down

Scope, price and timeline are agreed in writing, so nobody is surprised later.

Stay available

When something breaks at month end or term end, you can reach the people who built it.
